title: Raw rationalization and point-section interpretation of integral finite-fibre comparisons
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0=\mathbf F_q,k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For a scheme $W$, write $R_W=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_W$ on the small pro-etale site $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use $D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$ of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], the strict derived reductions $K_n=K\otimes^L_{R_W}(A_n)_W$, and exact restriction of scalars $\operatorname{Res}_n$ [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Let $Rf_*$ be the tower direct image of [def-weil-derived-direct-image].

For a geometric point $y:s=\operatorname{Spec}k\to Y$ [def-weil-geometric-point], set $S=X\times_Ys$ with projections $v:S\to X$, $h:S\to s$ [def-pc-base-change], and $P_y=\{x:s\to X\mid fx=y\}$. For $x\in P_y$ let $i_x:s\to S$ be the unique lift, so $vi_x=x$ and $hi_x=\operatorname{id}_s$. This is a finite set; an empty sum indexed by $P_y$ is the zero object. Write $L(-)^*$ for the completed integral pullback of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], and $(-)_n^*$ for its exact finite-coefficient inverse image.

On every one of $X,Y,S,s$, the category $D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$ agrees, with its completed ring sheaf and reduction functors, with the bounded constructible complete category [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. Its rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] is therefore the identical raw category of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]: objects are integral objects and morphisms are $\operatorname{Hom}(-,-)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$, with no idempotents adjoined. The rational standard pair [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure] is the localized integral pair; localization is t-exact and every object of its heart has an integral heart representative.

Suppose an $\mathcal O_E$-linear exact integral functor $T:D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)\to D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ preserves both halves of the standard pair and is equipped with specified natural integral isomorphisms
$$\beta_K:Ly^*TK\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_*Lv^*K,\qquad
\rho_K:Rh_*Lv^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_{x\in P_y}Lx^*K$$
whose strict reduction maps are, respectively, the exchange counit and the individual counit-germ restrictions. Assume $T$ is identified with the integral tower direct image by a comparison preserving every reduction projection. Its unique raw rational extension $T_E$ is the prescribed functor $Rf_*$ at $E$ [def-weil-derived-direct-image], and is t-exact. Its restriction $T_E^\heartsuit$ to the constructible heart [def-weil-constructible-heart] is exact. The localized $\beta,\rho$ give isomorphisms of derived objects over $s$.

For every rational heart object $\mathcal F$, applying termwise sections on $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$, then taking degree zero, identifies precisely these two maps with the restriction arrows
$$(T_E^\heartsuit\mathcal F)_y\xrightarrow{\sim}H^0(S,\mathcal F_S)\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_{x\in P_y}\mathcal F_x.$$
Here $\mathcal F_S=Lv^*\mathcal F$ in the heart, the point-fibre and stalk conventions are [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point, def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], and ordinary cohomology is [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. Point sections are exact and preserve the displayed finite biproduct; all three pullbacks have their heart interpretations. The identifications are natural in $\mathcal F$ and $E$-linear.

source.place: Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.8.14(2) and Remark 6.8.15; identification of the raw rational categories and point-section interpretation of the two integral restrictions, returned steps 8–9.

proof.text: The schemes $X,Y,s$ are finite type over the field $k$. The fibre $S$ is finite over $s$: on an affine neighborhood $\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $y$, with finite preimage $\operatorname{Spec}C$, its algebra is $C\otimes_Bk$, generated over $k$ by the images of finitely many $B$-module generators of $C$. Thus $S$ is finite type too. The $k$-algebra $C\otimes_Bk$ is spanned as a $k$-vector space by those finitely many images, so it is finite-dimensional, hence Artinian with finitely many maximal ideals, each with residue field finite over the algebraically closed $k$, hence equal to $k$. By the universal property of $S=X\times_Ys$, a point $x:s\to X$ with $fx=y$ is the same as a $k$-morphism $i_x:s\to S$ (a section of $h$), unique with $vi_x=x$; these correspond to the maximal ideals of $C\otimes_Bk$, so $P_y$ is finite (empty when $y$ is not in the image of $f$). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] over the noetherian field $k$ and [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] to all four schemes. The integer $\ell$ is a unit on them since $\ell\ne p$. The characterization [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] therefore applies: it explicitly says that the two integral categories in the statement select the same objects in the same ambient derived category, with the same completed ring sheaf and reductions. Both are full subcategories, so their morphisms, composition and integral standard cohomological classes agree as well.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11 and Proposition 6.8.11(3); project completed-category characterization, with its compatible witnesses and uniform bounds.

proof.text: For each of the four schemes, [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and [def-weil-pbc-rational-category] now apply the same operation to this same full integral category: they keep its objects and replace every morphism module by $\operatorname{Hom}(K,L)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$. The identities, composition and shift are consequently identical. The distinguished triangles are images of integral triangles and their isomorphic copies in either presentation. No Karoubi operation occurs. By [prop-weil-localized-tstructure] the rational classes are the isomorphism closures of the integral classes, localization is t-exact, and every rational heart object is isomorphic to the image of an integral heart object. These are exactly the classes of [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure], under Step 1's identification.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2); raw scalar localization and its localized standard t-structure.

proof.text: Apply [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] to the supplied integral functor and its specified comparison with the tower direct image. Explicitly $T_E(K)=TK$ and $T_E(u\otimes a)=T(u)\otimes a$. Every morphism is a fraction $u/\varpi^m$, so this is the unique $E$-linear extension. The comparison localizes with its actual components; by [def-weil-derived-direct-image], the rational direct image is this extension of the integral tower functor. Hence it identifies $T_E$ with the prescribed $Rf_*$. The same transport sends the given maps and their inverses to $\beta_K\otimes1$, $\rho_K\otimes1$ and their localized inverses. These are isomorphisms of derived objects before any sections or degree-zero operation. We retain the supplied maps themselves and their projection normalization; we do not choose new maps from separate finite-level equalities.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2) and Remark 6.8.15; transport of supplied exact integral functors and natural comparisons.

proof.text: If $M$ belongs to either rational standard class, choose an integral representative in that class as in Step 2. Its image under $T$ is in the same integral class by hypothesis, so $T_E M$ is in the same rational class. Thus $T_E$ is t-exact. For a short exact sequence in the heart, [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](4) gives a distinguished triangle with its three terms in the heart. The exact functor $T_E$ carries it to a distinguished triangle, still with three heart terms; the converse assertion of that same lemma gives a short exact sequence. This proves exactness of $T_E^\heartsuit$.

source.place: Localized t-structure from Proposition 6.8.14(2); heart exactness via distinguished triangles.

proof.text: For $g=y,v,x$, [lem-a1-integral-pullback-completed-comparison] identifies the actual integral pullback used here with the completed pullback, preserving every reduction projection and shifts. Under Step 1's category identification, [lem-per-integral-pullback-bounds] applies to these morphisms between noetherian finite-dimensional schemes with $\ell$ invertible: the completed functor preserves constructibility and both integral standard classes. The argument of Step 4, applied to each pullback and its raw extension, gives rational t-exactness. Thus for an integral heart representative $F_0$ of $\mathcal F$, the objects $Ly^*TF_0$, $Lv^*F_0$ and $Lx^*F_0$ have their indicated integral heart interpretations, and their images give the asserted rational heart interpretations.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.9(4)-(5), Proposition 6.6.11; the projection-normalized comparison of the two completed pullback models.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact], termwise $\Gamma(s,-)$ is exact on modules over $R_s$ and satisfies $H^i\Gamma(s,N)=\Gamma(s,\mathcal H^iN)$. Evaluation is additive, so it carries the finite biproduct's inclusions and projections to maps satisfying the same biproduct identities; for an empty index set it carries zero to zero. At $E$, [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point](3) prescribes $\operatorname{Fib}_s(QN)=\Gamma(s,N)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$. By [lem-weil-l-adic-integers-localization-uniformizer] this tensor is localization at $\varpi$. For any module map $d$, a fraction $z/\varpi^m$ lies in the localized kernel precisely when $\varpi^rdz=0$ for some $r$; it then has the cycle representative $\varpi^rz/\varpi^{m+r}$. Images are the fractions of images. This proves directly that localization commutes with kernels, images and cohomology. Point evaluation is consequently t-exact on the localized pair and preserves the same finite biproduct comparison.

source.place: Stacks Tags 0982 and 098H (proetale.tex, lemma-w-local-strictly-henselian-extremally-disconnected and lemma-w-contractible-is-weakly-contractible); point coefficient convention and fraction calculation.

proof.text: Apply $H^0\operatorname{Fib}_s$ to exactly the localized $\beta,\rho$ of Step 3. By [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] the first term is $(T_E^\heartsuit\mathcal F)_y$ and each final summand is $\mathcal F_x$. By [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], since $h:S\to s$ is the structure map, the middle term is precisely $H^0(S,Lv^*\mathcal F)=H^0(S,\mathcal F_S)$. Step 6 identifies the last term with $\bigoplus_x\mathcal F_x$, using its actual projections. Hence the displayed arrows are the sections and degree-zero images of the supplied exchange and individual counit-germ restrictions, rather than merely abstract isomorphisms between their endpoints. All constructions are functors. Naturality holds first for an integral morphism $u$ by the supplied naturality squares, and for $u/\varpi^m$ by multiplying those same squares by $\varpi^{-m}$. Choosing an isomorphism $QF_0\cong\mathcal F$ transports those squares to every rational heart object; naturality makes the result independent of the representative. The same formulas prove $E$-linearity. The zero complex and the empty fibre give the unique maps between zero objects.
